clue.text: Senior ministers, cunning men in a tactical game

parts.note: arch means knowing or sly
bishops are pieces in chess

explanation.surface: Crafty players in a strategy game are being likened to senior government ministers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Men' is the usual crossword word for chess pieces, and the bishop is one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Archbishops are the highest-ranking clergy, ministers of the church in the religious sense.

clue.text: Striking article, really going into pronouns

parts.note: the indefinite article

indicators.note: going into something means entering it, so this piece sits inside the next

parts.note: two pronouns, we and me
so as in very, really

explanation.surface: A grammar note about an article going in among pronouns, called really striking.
explanation.definitionFit: Something awesome inspires awe, so it is impressive or striking.

clue.text: One that's agreed to share the bill in coffee shop runs

definitions.text: One that's agreed to share the bill

parts.note: Costa Coffee is a British chain of coffee shops
the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone agrees to split the bill at a coffee shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Share the bill' suggests splitting a café tab, but the bill here is the list of actors billed for a show.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-star shares top billing with another lead performer in a film or play.

clue.text: Member of a ropey team that plays for the church

definitions.text: Member of a ropey team that plays for the church

parts.note: surface: a player in a poor side, ropey being British slang for shoddy
cryptic: a team that pulls ropes to sound the church tower

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ropey' means poor quality in British slang, hinting at a bad parish sports side; read literally it is a team working with ropes.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell-ringer is one of a band who pull ropes to ring the bells of a church tower.

clue.text: Story of a rabbit getting comeuppance

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means reading from the bottom upwards

parts.note: taken as written
to rabbit is British slang for chatting at length, as is to gas

explanation.surface: A tale in which a rabbit finally gets its just deserts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit' is the verb, British slang for talk on and on, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long narrative, originally a Norse heroic tale, so a story.

clue.text: Cancel extra trip

parts.note: over as in left over, in excess
a ride is a short journey

explanation.surface: An instruction to call off an additional journey.
explanation.definitionFit: To override a decision is to set it aside or annul it, which is to cancel it.

clue.text: Do scruffier manoeuvres, having lost both rooks

indicators.note: manoeuvres are moves that shift things about, so the letters are rearranged
having lost means something is taken away from the word

parts.note: taken as written
R is the chess notation for rook; both of them are removed

explanation.surface: A chess player's messier moves are enough once both rooks are gone.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing both Rs leaves SCUFFIE to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: 'That will do' means that will be enough, the sense in which to suffice is to do.

clue.text: Insult unsettled touring English opener?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters travel round the next piece, enclosing it
unsettled things are disturbed out of their order, so the word before it is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: An English opening batsman on an overseas tour is unsettled by an insult from the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English opener' suggests a cricketer; the question mark flags that the definition is really 'opener', as in a tin opener.
explanation.definitionFit: A tin or bottle opener is an example of a kitchen utensil, hence the question mark.

clue.text: A Parisian in Hello! snapped by top journalist, 18

definitions.note: refers to the answer at 18 across, FREE

parts.note: the French for a
taken as written
a greeting
a dog that snapped bit
ED, short for editor, the top journalist on a paper

explanation.surface: A Parisian appearing in Hello! magazine gets photographed by a leading journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snapped' suggests a photographer, but it means bit. 18 across is FREE, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone uninhibited is free of restraint or self-consciousness, so free in manner.

clue.text: Visiting Honolulu, feel good about showing happiness

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the letters are read from right to left
the answer is a visitor staying inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the letters straddling the end of Honolulu, all of feel and the start of good

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker in Hawaii feels good about the trip.
explanation.definitionFit: Being gleeful means visibly delighted, so it describes someone showing happiness.

clue.text: Blonde speaker's delay is insignificant

parts.note: blonde hair is light in colour

indicators.note: what a speaker says is heard, not seen, so the next word counts by its sound

parts.note: a delay is a wait, which sounds like a unit of heaviness

explanation.surface: A fair-haired speaker's late arrival is said to be of no importance.
explanation.definitionFit: A lightweight figure carries little influence or importance, the figurative sense of insignificant.

clue.text: I would love Hollywood perhaps, and seek adoration

parts.note: contracted to I'd
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
Hollywood is part of Los Angeles
to seek is to try or attempt

explanation.surface: A would-be star longs for Hollywood and the adoration that comes with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Idolatry is excessive worship or admiration of something, which is adoration taken to an extreme.

clue.text: Tough, sturdy signage that falls down occasionally

indicators.note: occasionally means only now and then, so every other letter of the words before is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on

explanation.surface: A supposedly sturdy sign keeps falling down now and then, which is a nuisance.
explanation.definitionFit: A trying time or a trying person is hard to cope with, so tough in the sense of difficult.

clue.text: One's time is nearly at hand

definitions.text: One's time is nearly at hand

parts.words: One's time is nearly at hand
parts.note: surface: someone's moment is almost here
cryptic: a device that shows the time, sitting just beside the hand on the arm

explanation.walkthrough: 'At hand' means imminent in the surface; literally it places the timepiece next to the hand.
explanation.definitionFit: A timepiece worn on a strap just above the hand shows the hour, so its time is almost at the hand.

clue.text: 'Pay attention,' the man had announced

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: the man had is contracted to he'd

explanation.surface: A man calls out for everyone to listen to him.
explanation.definitionFit: To heed is to take notice of or attend to a warning, which means the same as paying attention.

clue.text: Rewrite for re-editing, taking in new part

indicators.note: taking in means absorbing, so the rearranged letters hold the next piece
rewriting reorders the material, so the hyphenated word is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, hyphen dropped
standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: An editor's instruction: rewrite this passage for the second edit, incorporating new material.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingredient is one component of a mixture or recipe, so a part of the whole.

clue.text: Unusual ceramic container for Eastern sweet delight

indicators.note: the rearranged letters form a vessel that holds the next piece
something unusual is out of the normal order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
standard abbreviation for Eastern

explanation.surface: An unusual pottery dish is used to serve an Eastern dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Ice cream is a frozen sweet dessert, a treat many find delightful.

clue.text: He clues 'Bee' cryptically: 'It's yellow with streaks'

indicators.note: a cryptic treatment twists the words, so the quoted letters are rearranged

parts.note: all the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A setter clues the word Bee with a hint about a yellow insect with stripes.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition looks like it describes a bee's stripes, but it describes pale cheese veined with blue mould.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue cheese such as Stilton is a creamy yellowish cheese marbled with blue-green veins of mould.

clue.text: Hooks up or loosens laces maybe, if entering for tango

indicators.note: coming in for something means taking its place, so one piece swaps out another

parts.note: undoing shoelaces is one example of untying
taken as written
T is tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone either ties up or loosens shoelaces, perhaps before dancing a tango.
explanation.definitionFit: To unify things is to join them together, which is to hook them up.

clue.text: Price is about right? Certainly, if it's this

definitions.text: Price is about right? Certainly, if it's this

indicators.note: being about something means going round it, so the price word encloses the next piece

parts.note: a fee is a price charged
standard abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a price is fair and is told it certainly is, if nothing is charged.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer: a price is undeniably right when it costs nothing. The first four words also build it.
explanation.definitionFit: Anything costing nothing has a price nobody can complain about, so the whole clue describes something gratis.

clue.text: Put out again about one's appeal

parts.note: re means concerning, about
one is I, so one's is I's
to sue is to appeal or petition

explanation.surface: Someone republishes something to do with their own appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: To reissue a book or record is to publish or release it a second time.

clue.text: Starters for dinner everyone just ate voraciously — usual familiar experience?

indicators.note: starters are what come first, so only the opening letter of each word counts

parts.words: dinner everyone just ate voraciously — usual
parts.note: the initial letters of these six words

explanation.surface: At dinner everyone wolfed the starters as they always do, which feels familiar.
explanation.definitionFit: Déjà vu is the uncanny feeling that a new experience has happened before, so it feels familiar.

clue.text: Start with what's necessary to outwit champion

indicators.note: what is necessary to something is an essential part of it, so the answer is a piece found inside the words that follow

parts.note: the end of outwit runs on into the start of champion

explanation.surface: Advice on how to begin if you want to get the better of a champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start' reads like an instruction to begin, but it is the definition, meaning a sudden jerk or jump.
explanation.definitionFit: A start is a sudden involuntary jump of surprise, and a twitch is a small sudden jerk.

clue.text: Radical son in tears

parts.note: standard abbreviation for son
someone in tears is weeping

explanation.surface: A rebellious son is reduced to tears.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweeping changes are wide-ranging and far-reaching, the same as radical ones.

clue.text: After getting up, small number will go to church

indicators.note: in a down entry, getting up means reading from the bottom upwards

parts.note: NO is the short form of number
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: After rising in the morning, a small congregation heads off to church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' looks like part of the instruction, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Once can mean as soon as or after, as in once you have eaten, you may leave.

clue.text: Doctor with single tube of blood attended by vehicle

parts.note: standard abbreviation for doctor
the Roman numeral for one
a vein is a vessel carrying blood

explanation.surface: A doctor arrives by car carrying a single vial of blood.
explanation.definitionFit: A drive-in cinema or restaurant is one that customers attend while sitting in their cars.

clue.text: Tons moved — rest in van

parts.note: standard abbreviation for tons
ran as in moved quickly
to sit is to rest

explanation.surface: Tons of goods have been shifted, with the rest stowed in the van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moved' looks like an anagram signal, but it simply gives a past tense meaning went.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ford Transit is a widely used British van, so its model name stands for the vehicle.

clue.text: Mathematician with pipe sent outside of university building

parts.note: jokily, one who does sums

indicators.note: a thing sent outside something else ends up surrounding it

parts.note: a hose is a flexible pipe
standard abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A maths don with a pipe is sent out of the university building.
explanation.walkthrough: SUMMER is read as someone who sums rather than the season.
explanation.definitionFit: A summerhouse is a small garden building used for sitting in during warm weather.
